problem:
Given the set of functions ${x,\,{e}^{x},\,2x}$ defined on $x\in R,$ select the correct options in the following reasoning.For all $x\in R,$  we have that

$$
{{field-1}}\cdot x+{{field-2}}\cdot {e}^{x}+{{field-3}}\cdot 2x=0.
$$

Since

the scalar coefficients in the linear combination are zero, the given set of functions is linearly 
{{field-5}}.
worked_solution:
Recall that the set of functions ${{f}_{1}(x),{f}_{2}(x),…,{f}_{n}(x)},$ which are defined on some interval $I,$ is *linearly dependent* if there exist real scalars ${k}_{1},{k}_{2},…,{k}_{n}$ not all zero such that the linear combination ${k}_{1}\cdot {f}_{1}+{k}_{2}\cdot {f}_{2}+…+{k}_{n}\cdot {f}_{n}$ is identically zero, i.e, 

$$
{k}_{1}\cdot {f}_{1}(x)+{k}_{2}\cdot {f}_{2}(x)+…+{k}_{n}\cdot {f}_{n}(x)=0
$$

for all $x\in I.$ Otherwise, if ${k}_{1}={k}_{2}=⋯={k}_{n}=0$ is the only solution, the set is *linearly independent*.

Now, for all $x\in R,$ we have that 

$$
2\cdot x+0\cdot {e}^{x}+(-1)\cdot 2x=0.
$$

Therefore, since $\text{not all}$ the scalar coefficients in the linear combination are zero, the given set of functions is linearly $\text{dependent}.$

EXPLANATION

Recall that the set of functions {f1(x),f2(x),…,fn(x)}, which are defined on some interval I, is linearly dependent if there exist real scalars k1,k2,…,kn not all zero such that the linear combination k1⋅f1+k2⋅f2+…+kn⋅fn is identically zero, i.e, k1⋅f1(x)+k2⋅f2(x)+…+kn⋅fn(x)=0 for all x∈I. Otherwise, if k1=k2=⋯=kn=0 is the only solution, the set is linearly independent.

Now, for all x∈R, we have that 2⋅x+0⋅ex+(−1)⋅2x=0.

Therefore, since not all the scalar coefficients in the linear combination are zero, the given set of functions is linearly dependent.
